archive_03_001.speaker: narrator
archive_03_001.text: The school stove passed its test on the eighth morning. The carpenter checked the new pipe's joints, watched the draught and waited through a full ordinary firing before signing the return to use. The teacher led the children down after lunch. Their stools went back to the lender, the cook recovered her kettle and Luo rolled up the mountain screen. A boy asked to take the blue sheep home. Luo offered him the painter's name instead, and the boy decided his own slate was sufficient.

archive_03_002.speaker: narrator
archive_03_002.text: Quiet in the receiving room proved stranger than the lesson noise. The floor had dried into a map of pale boot marks, and the borrowed room seemed briefly abandoned. Yue helped remove the chalk dust with damp cloths before any records returned to the tables. Tan found a slate pencil wedged against a screen leg. She placed it in the lost-property bowl rather than allowing it to roll beneath the cabinets. The archive had acquired one useful public episode and several small obligations that would outlast its notice.

archive_03_003.speaker: narrator
archive_03_003.text: Dai used the cleared table to spread the roof estimate. The carpenter priced the structural work at nine hundred and eighty copper. The archive's restricted repair reserve held two hundred and sixty. Its pending seasonal grant asked for seven hundred and twenty, completing the estimate without drawing on wages, meals or travel already committed under staff appointments. Yue checked the addition and then the price dates. Slate transport would become dearer after the first hard frost. The council had not yet decided, and the estimate would remain open for only twelve more days.

archive_03_004.speaker: narrator
archive_03_004.text: Luo's draft letter described the archive's public use, including the borrowed classroom and corrected school accounts. Dai crossed out a sentence claiming the archive had restored justice to the teacher. A corrected debt, she wrote, was a specific result they could document. Justice might require the daughter to receive the correction and stop fearing another demand. Luo accepted the change with a sigh that suggested he had grown fond of his sentence. Yue made the clean copy without smuggling its splendid claim into a different paragraph.

archive_03_005.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_03_005.text: The council wants a reason to spend money where the road is expensive. A roof estimate tells it how much; a public use tells it why. I am trying to answer both questions before winter answers them for us. But Dai is right about that sentence. The teacher's daughter is a person receiving a letter, not the final line of my application. I can name the classroom, the corrected entries and the opening hours. They are less stirring, and they will survive someone asking to see the proof.

archive_03_006.speaker: narrator
archive_03_006.text: The orchard representative arrived the next day before the comparison hour. She had come on foot despite owning a share in the trustees' cart hire. Her coat was patched at both elbows. At the gate she asked where the school children had gone, then looked relieved to hear about the inspected flue. This was not the formidable proprietor He had described in the kitchen. Yue reminded herself that a patched coat could conceal either generosity or thrift, and a pleasant arrival did not resolve a dispute.

archive_03_007.speaker: narrator
archive_03_007.text: He came with his mother carrying the same admitted copy, supported between two clean boards. He had removed his courier straps and put on a jacket whose cuffs had been lengthened with different cloth. The representative recognised his mother and asked about a neighbour's bad leg. Their exchange lasted only three sentences, but it unsettled He more than an accusation would have. The people denying the house were people who could remember who had brought soup during an illness. He looked toward Yue as if asking how an enemy could arrive with such ordinary facts.

archive_03_008.speaker: narrator
archive_03_008.text: The comparison began with the original's condition. Tan placed it on a low support, kept its fragile fold from bearing its own weight and adjusted the light until the writing could be read without lifting the sheet toward the window. Yue copied the relevant clauses into two columns. Dai read each aloud while the parties looked at their own sources. The earliest original granted the grandmother occupation for her lifetime. It gave no automatic right to descendants. The copy He brought contained an additional paragraph below that grant.

archive_03_009.speaker: narrator
archive_03_009.text: The added paragraph assigned continued occupation to descendants who maintained the school path and its drainage. Its handwriting matched the earlier text in the retained copy, but that only established what the copyist had copied onto this particular sheet. The copy bore a later date and a witness name. It lacked the registrar's endorsement that would normally connect an amendment to the earlier filed deed. He pointed to the witness name immediately. His mother had known the man. The orchard representative knew him too, and neither memory supplied the missing endorsement.

archive_03_010.speaker: narrator
archive_03_010.text: The representative's account was less simple than refusal. The house had stood empty for two winters after He's grandmother died. Orchard funds replaced part of its roof and repaired a broken lower wall. The trustees then let it to an elderly orchard worker at a low rent, using that rent for the school's boundary fence. The worker still lived there. Returning possession to He would therefore displace a person, unwind a use of money and settle whether the trustees had ever possessed the right they had exercised.

archive_03_011.speaker: he_xi
archive_03_011.text: When I picture the house, I picture my grandmother sitting beside its door. I do not picture an old worker who needs somewhere dry. I know that is unfair, but hearing about him has not made my grandmother's door less real. My mother asked about moving back while the house was still empty, and she was told there was no right left to ask about. If the trustees repaired it afterwards, I need the hearing to know that we were not simply absent until the roof became useful again.

archive_03_012.speaker: narrator
archive_03_012.text: His mother confirmed the earlier request. The representative had not been on the committee at that time. She knew the roof payment but had seen no record of the family's enquiry. Dai listed the enquiry as a disputed event requiring sources, separate from the text comparison. The list grew without becoming an accusation sheet. Yue wrote the old worker's present occupation beside the question about possession. He watched her and asked whether the worker would receive notice before anyone promised He a key. She said that question should be put to the registrar handling the hearing.

archive_03_013.speaker: narrator
archive_03_013.text: Luo brought in the public endowment amendment authorising the school path across the orchard. Its date fell between the original deed and He's retained copy. It promised the school permanent passage and assigned routine drain clearance to the occupant of the lower house. It did not itself identify that occupant's inheritance rights. The copy's later clause could have been intended to connect the two obligations, but intention would need a lawful instrument. Three writings now described one stretch of ground, and each answered a different part of the difficulty.

archive_03_014.speaker: narrator
archive_03_014.text: He wanted to know who had held the pen that made his copy. The witnessed date suggested the founder was still alive. Dai checked the accession register, which recorded a packet of amendments received during the founder's final autumn. Its list mentioned a school-path agreement and a house continuation paper as separate items. The catalogue cabinet contained only the school-path number. The house paper's number pointed to a former shelf designation no longer in use. Dai rested her finger beside the empty location field and did not pretend she had overlooked it lightly.

archive_03_015.speaker: narrator
archive_03_015.text: The missing location was not new damage. A cabinet reorganisation seven years earlier had compressed several accession descriptions, and this particular number had been dropped while the earlier original retained its place. Dai's signature appeared on the reorganisation approval. She read it aloud herself. The task had been supervised by a predecessor whose eyesight was failing, but she had accepted responsibility for the completed cabinet. Luo's eyes moved from the signature to her face. He had argued with her about access for years; this was the first time she could not answer a request by pointing to a known location.

archive_03_016.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_03_016.text: This is an archive failure before it is evidence for either inheritance position. I signed a move record that no longer gives a traceable destination for an admitted item. We will search the listed receiving shelves and movement registers in the order they name. I will preserve the wrong card as evidence of the break. He, it would be understandable to want my error to prove your copy correct. It does not do that yet. It does give you a reason to require someone besides me to check what we do next.

archive_03_017.speaker: narrator
archive_03_017.text: The orchard representative agreed to an independent record of the search. She also asked Dai not to make He pay the standard retrieval fee for an item the archive had lost track of. Dai accepted that without consulting Luo. The archive's operational error allowance would cover the paid search work within the appointments already in place; any extra hours would need a separate authorisation. Yue noticed that the representative wrote the waiver down in her own notebook. It was a small action on behalf of the family whose larger claim she opposed.

archive_03_018.speaker: narrator
archive_03_018.text: They ended the session with no declared authentic version. The parties took their own admitted papers home. The original returned to its guarded support, and the accession register remained on the work table for the approved search. The orchard representative undertook to notify the current house occupant about a possible formal hearing through the district registrar, without suggesting that eviction had been decided. He asked her to preserve repair invoices as well as rent receipts. She agreed. Both requests recognised that even a rightful outcome would need to account for events already lived.

archive_03_019.speaker: narrator
archive_03_019.text: Yue found He beside the outer steps after the session. He was trying to tie his carrying strap with the fine new cuff caught in the knot. She held the loose cloth while he freed it. They stood looking down toward the house whose roof was barely visible through the trees. He said he had wanted someone to confess something. Dai had confessed an archival failure, but it was not the crime he had prepared himself to hear. He did not know whether to be disappointed or grateful that the representative had waived his fee.

archive_03_020.speaker: lin_yue
archive_03_020.text: You can leave those feelings in the same room for a while. You do not have to choose one before we begin the search. I will be working from the movement record, not from an answer I want to hand you. If we find the house paper, it may make the question easier or harder. If we cannot find it, the broken catalogue will still need correction. You should not have to keep returning merely so that we remember we once misplaced something you needed.

archive_03_021.speaker: narrator
archive_03_021.text: The search occupied the tenth day. Yue and a clerk began with the old-to-new shelf list while Tan prepared supports for any packet they might need to open. Dai kept to the separate task of checking the accession entries against a second register, giving the search less dependence on her interpretation of her own old approval. Luo arranged for a council clerk to witness the handling record at the next ordinary visit. He could not summon an independent official by announcing one, but he could reserve a visit already scheduled for grant inspection.

archive_03_022.speaker: narrator
archive_03_022.text: The first receiving shelf held school rental agreements, not the house continuation paper. Its packet count matched the move record exactly. The second shelf had a box whose label concealed an earlier number beneath loose paste. Tan lifted the loose label edge without removing the old writing. The box had moved twice, each time with a count but no item list. Dai had once trusted a count as enough because the boxes remained tied. The workroom now showed how a tied box could carry an unnamed error safely from cabinet to cabinet.

archive_03_023.speaker: narrator
archive_03_023.text: A long pencil rubbed away the grit from the box's underside. Yue supported the base while the clerk cut the outer working tie recorded during the last move. They found lease renewals, three orchard fence plans and a folded inventory of a retired steward's furniture. None was the missing instrument. The clerk looked almost offended by the furniture. Dai asked him to catalogue it properly before resealing the permitted packet. A disappointing search result could still expose another object which had spent years living beneath the wrong description.

archive_03_024.speaker: narrator
archive_03_024.text: The day ended with three locations checked and none resolved. Dai's face grew more controlled as the list of failures lengthened. Luo offered to continue after supper. Tan refused because the handling room's natural light had gone and the prepared lamps were needed for the scheduled copy work. Yue was relieved to stop, then ashamed of the relief until Tan handed her a bowl of water for washing. Searching required good hands tomorrow. Fatigue was not evidence that the missing document had become more important after dusk.

archive_03_025.speaker: narrator
archive_03_025.text: The cook had obtained bruised orchard apples cheaply and was making a thick stew of them. He carried a paid note from the representative confirming that the repair records would be preserved. He refused another delivery offered for the same evening because the weather was worsening along the lower track. The requester objected that the destination was visible from the yard. He pointed toward the two bends hidden by trees and quoted a morning rate. The cook gave him an apple portion larger than anyone else's and called it a consultation fee.

archive_03_026.speaker: narrator
archive_03_026.text: On the eleventh morning, the roof inspector reached the mountain earlier than expected. He worked for the grant council and had come with the ordinary clerk Luo had contacted. The first part of their visit concerned damaged beams and the carpenter's estimate. The clerk then witnessed the search register, confirming what had been checked and the point where the old move list stopped naming individual contents. Neither visitor could decide the house claim. Their signatures proved their own observations, and Dai looked unexpectedly steadier after those limited things were written.

archive_03_027.speaker: narrator
archive_03_027.text: The inspector's report confirmed the repair estimate but added a condition: the winter hall's northern bay should close before heavy snow unless the beam work finished. The hall held public reading tables and a wall of deposits behind a separate locked screen. Closing it would remove most winter access even if the papers survived elsewhere. Luo's grant case became more urgent at precisely the moment Dai's mislaid accession made the council clerk doubtful about institutional management. She answered the clerk's questions instead of asking him to admire her concern.

archive_03_028.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_03_028.text: The papers may remain legible while the system for finding them fails. We have evidence of that failure in the house accession. The proposed roof work will not correct it, and correcting the cabinet will not keep snow off a weakened beam. I am asking the council to consider both obligations separately. If it requires a supervised management plan with the grant, I will prepare one. Please do not describe a closed winter reading hall as harmless because the locked screen behind it still protects the deposits.

archive_03_029.speaker: narrator
archive_03_029.text: The clerk wanted current visitor numbers and winter opening arrangements. Luo supplied the ordinary logs, including refusals when the receiving room was occupied or the requested record was restricted. He did not inflate school pupils into separate research visitors. The inspector laughed at the blue sheep story, but left it out of his report. Yue copied the roof figures once more and checked that the council's seven hundred and twenty request remained distinct from the operational wage account. The winter hall could not pay for itself by silently consuming people already contracted to work there.

archive_03_030.speaker: narrator
archive_03_030.text: That afternoon the old steward's furniture inventory supplied an unexpected lead. The last item named a narrow drawer transferred with a reading desk to the winter hall. Its margin listed three small paper packets stored inside, including the same former shelf designation as the missing house number. The drawer itself had been removed during a later leg repair and placed on a high maintenance shelf. Yue brought Dai the reference rather than rushing toward the hall. Dai read it twice, then asked Tan to assess the shelf access.

archive_03_031.speaker: narrator
archive_03_031.text: The maintenance shelf was in a safe bay, reached by an ordinary platform inspected for the task. Tan climbed while Yue steadied the empty receiving tray on a lower bench. The drawer contained an iron hinge, a worn spectacles case and two tied packets. A third packet's paper outline remained in the dust, but the packet was gone. The tied packets proved to be annual lease receipts. Yue's hopeful breath turned into a cough. Tan descended with the permitted items and the handling note describing the empty third space without claiming to know when it became empty.

archive_03_032.speaker: narrator
archive_03_032.text: Luo asked whether anyone might have taken the third packet to correct the shortened catalogue seven years earlier. Dai checked the maintenance book for the desk repair. A dated entry said three packets had been removed, two returned and one sent to the reading steward for reference. Luo had held that office at the time. He stared at the words with a disbelief as naked as Dai's had been over her signature. His earlier impatience suddenly found an older version of himself waiting in the margin.

archive_03_033.speaker: narrator
archive_03_033.text: He remembered using an orchard paper to answer an enquiry about access to the school gate. He did not remember its accession number or returning it. The old reading-room daybook might supply the enquiry date, but that book had been packed among routine desk papers after a flood in the lower room. The flooded box was catalogued as unsorted office materials, and its contents could not be opened without Tan's assessment. Dai's expression changed neither to victory nor accusation. Yue thought Luo would have found either easier than the quiet request for the book's number.

archive_03_034.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_03_034.text: I was angry because your cabinet made people wait. I may have taken an instrument out of its proper place to answer someone quickly, then left the next person with a worse cabinet. I need to say that before I look for an excuse in the flood. Perhaps the book will show I returned it. Perhaps it will not. I will not be the only person recording that search. I still believe access matters. Today I have to discover what my own version of access cost someone else.

archive_03_035.speaker: narrator
archive_03_035.text: He arrived with a parcel for the grant clerk and found Luo sitting over the maintenance entry. Dai explained the lead in the presence of both parties' appointed contact, who had returned to collect the comparison record. She did not withhold Luo's possible involvement until it could be made less uncomfortable. He listened without interrupting. Afterwards he asked Luo whether the quick enquiry had been his mother's. Luo said he did not remember. The answer hurt more than a denial because it could contain a forgotten day around which a family had arranged years.

archive_03_036.speaker: narrator
archive_03_036.text: The daybook's box had not grown active mould, but its covers were fused by the old flood. Tan would not prise the book open while the paper remained rigid. She recommended a controlled assessment by the regional preservation office, which could lend the appropriate equipment and trained operator if the road stayed open. Sending the book down required a transport support and a custody receipt. Dai authorised the assessment from a small treatment allocation already available, choosing it before the next decorative catalogue printing. A new label could wait while an old request remained inaccessible.

archive_03_037.speaker: narrator
archive_03_037.text: Yue helped build the support with ordinary boards, clean cloth and spacers that kept the stiff covers from bearing transit shocks. He offered to carry the package down as a paid courier task because he knew the lower road. Dai declined to appoint him as sole carrier on a matter affecting his petition. He looked wounded until Luo explained the alternative: He could witness the sealing, keep the outward receipt and continue his unrelated route. A separately paid archive carrier would take the box, and a preservation clerk would acknowledge it below.

archive_03_038.speaker: narrator
archive_03_038.text: The representative accepted that arrangement and paid her own messenger to accompany the notification, not the book. She said the trustees wanted the source examined as badly as He did now that their house repair decisions might have relied on an unanswered enquiry. He asked whether wanting an examination meant accepting his claim. She answered no. He laughed without amusement, but this time he did not accuse her of hiding a bargain. They agreed to receive the same assessment report and preserve their separate copies of the submitted comparison.

archive_03_039.speaker: narrator
archive_03_039.text: Rain delayed the carrier by one morning. The twelve-day estimate deadline had only eight days left, and the council's answer was still descending through its ordinary meeting timetable. Luo paced the covered yard until the cook asked whether he was testing the paving. Dai sent a plain request for an interim roof decision, identifying the seasonal price deadline rather than claiming an immediate collapse. The weakened bay remained closed. Yue watched buckets fill in the other room and thought of the difference between a danger being urgent and a sentence making it sound louder.

archive_03_040.speaker: narrator
archive_03_040.text: On the thirteenth day, the school opened its repaired teaching room to parents. The stove glowed safely under the teacher's supervision, and the new pipe rose through a patched square brighter than the ceiling around it. Sun attended as a visitor because a child had invited her to hear his reading. She sat near the door and corrected no accounts. He came at his mother's request and stood beside the slate shelves. The path into the school was wet but draining. He began to notice each shallow channel as if seeing handwriting across the ground.

archive_03_041.speaker: narrator
archive_03_041.text: The teacher's daughter sent a reply acknowledging withdrawal of the debt and fee. She did not offer forgiveness to the archive or the school, and the trustee did not ask her to. She wanted the correction copied to the neighbouring lender who had once refused her because the school debt appeared on an account reference. The trustee agreed to send it under the daughter's chosen address and fields. A removed column did not instantly remove every place its shadow had reached. Luo placed the extra mailing on the follow-up list rather than calling the matter closed.

archive_03_042.speaker: narrator
archive_03_042.text: Yue copied the authorised correction during her next work period. She felt the small pressure of wanting the daughter to send a kinder answer. Then she looked at the dates of the earlier reminders. The daughter had spent those intervals with a demand Yue had helped end only last week. A clerk's relief at a completed correction was not the recipient's timetable. Yue addressed the second message carefully and kept the receipt with the school record. It would be useful even if the daughter never thanked anyone who wrote it.

archive_03_043.speaker: narrator
archive_03_043.text: The regional preservation office replied that the damaged daybook could be assessed within six working days, using its ordinary queue. It might yield the enquiry entry or remain unreadable in places. The carrier's custody receipt recorded both stiff covers, the tied support and the receiving clerk's name. Dai posted the receipt number in the search log. Luo stopped pacing for an afternoon and began opening his own old desk bundles with the clerk. There could be another note of the enquiry outside the daybook, and seeking it was work he could do without waiting for the book to become legible.

archive_03_044.speaker: narrator
archive_03_044.text: The bundles held plans for reader benches, unpaid lamp bills and drafts of a notice whose final version Luo had never liked. He found a scrap describing the orchard gate enquiry in his own hand. It referred to a house continuation leaf copied for a visitor, then returned to the drawer. The line could corroborate a return, but it named neither date nor visitor. Dai catalogued it as an undated desk note rather than letting it complete the movement chain. Luo touched the scrap with the back of one knuckle, as if uncertain it belonged to him.

archive_03_045.speaker: narrator
archive_03_045.text: The apparent return conflicted with the maintenance book's empty third space only if both described the same drawer at the same moment. They did not yet know that. Yue drew the known movements in ordinary pencil with blank intervals left visibly open. The clerk wanted arrows through the blanks, saying the story would be easier to read. She answered that the intervals were what they still needed to investigate. He agreed and added the dates they did have. The page became less graceful and more useful.

archive_03_046.speaker: narrator
archive_03_046.text: Tan inspected another public register while the daybook waited below. The archive could not suspend all preservation around one inheritance claim. This register held mountain birth entries written by several clerks in different inks. One ink had faded almost completely at the outer edge, leaving parents' names visible but dates faint. Tan explained that paper condition and writing condition required different descriptions. Yue practised copying the visible fields and leaving the dates unresolved. A birth did not become less real because she could not read its number, but a certified date could not be manufactured from that sympathy.

archive_03_047.speaker: tan_ke
archive_03_047.text: There are days when preservation feels like teaching people to live beside a hole. You support the leaf, stop the leak and tell them which words have already gone. They want a ladder into the missing place, and sometimes a better lamp helps. Sometimes nothing does. I have to be honest without enjoying the honesty as a kind of superior sadness. These entries belong to people who may still need a date. When the page fails them, our next task is to identify other lawful sources, not admire the failure.

archive_03_048.speaker: narrator
archive_03_048.text: The birth register's request concerned a mill apprentice who needed proof of age for a paid position. Luo contacted the apprentice's appointed village registrar about the ordinary alternative certificate process. The archive supplied the surviving entry fields and described the unreadable date. Yue did not see the resulting application; it belonged to the apprentice. She saw only the dispatch receipt and the note that a different source could be checked. Work continued around the missing house paper, and its continuation kept the archive from becoming a single family's haunted room.

archive_03_049.speaker: narrator
archive_03_049.text: He began taking morning courier routes again. His mother wanted him to remain available for every new search development. He told her the archive could send a message to his route station, and that waiting in the yard would not make the daybook dry. They argued quietly by the outer gate. Yue moved her box trolley past without slowing. Later He apologised to the cook for speaking sharply when she asked whether he wanted lunch. The cook accepted the apology and made him sit until he had eaten enough to stop chewing his own temper.

archive_03_050.speaker: narrator
archive_03_050.text: The representative returned with the house repair invoices. Under their comparison agreement, the clerk copied relevant totals and work descriptions while leaving unrelated orchard accounts covered. The roof repair had been real and ordinarily priced. The lower wall invoice included an urgent drainage trench cut across the school's path. That trench explained why He's mother remembered clearing the drain twice in one spring. It also revealed that part of the trustees' house expenditure had served the school's common access. The representative asked for that distinction to be preserved if costs ever entered a settlement.

archive_03_051.speaker: narrator
archive_03_051.text: Dai admitted it. He studied the trench drawing and admitted that his mother had not rebuilt the damaged wall herself. The modest exchange cost them both something. He could no longer imagine the trustees as merely collecting rent from a house his family alone had maintained. The representative could no longer treat the path work as a vague claim with no physical relation to her own invoices. Yue wrote the agreed factual points in a third column. Agreement did not need to swallow the remaining dispute in order to be worth keeping.

archive_03_052.speaker: narrator
archive_03_052.text: The council's interim reply arrived on the sixteenth day. It would release the seven hundred and twenty grant if the archive accepted supervised procurement, a public winter access schedule and an annual review of its catalogue movement records. It did not require opening private deposits. Dai read the terms twice, seeking a hidden access demand. Luo found none. The carpenter could begin within three days if they ordered materials immediately. The archive's two hundred and sixty reserve completed the funding, and the total stayed exactly at the nine hundred and eighty estimate.

archive_03_053.speaker: narrator
archive_03_053.text: The council also asked for a revised winter operating plan before the first frost. Repair money would pay beams, slates, transport and labour under the estimate. It would not pay for extra heating months or extend Yue's thirty-six-day appointment. Those questions belonged to the archive's operational account and governing board. Luo's relief therefore lasted one cup of tea before becoming another list. Dai set the grant beside the repair reserve ledger and authorised procurement. The carpenter, who had been waiting to hear a number rather than a metaphor, shook hands with both of them.

archive_03_054.speaker: narrator
archive_03_054.text: Yue helped the clerk prepare the order list, using the carpenter's quantities rather than converting the grant into an unspecified abundance of materials. Slate and beam suppliers required deposits, the carter required a confirmed route and the council wanted receipts before releasing the final portion. The archive's reserve could bridge the first deposits while the initial grant payment travelled. Dai recorded that timing openly so the reserve would not appear spent twice. He accepted a paid delivery carrying the order confirmations, with his ordinary route still subject to weather assessment.

archive_03_055.speaker: narrator
archive_03_055.text: That evening Luo opened the winter hall's safe southern tables for a short public reading hour. The northern bay remained screened and closed pending the repair. Sunset touched the covered shelves with a warmth their paper did not absorb. An elderly visitor read a copied grazing right beside a young man checking his grandfather's tax exemption. Neither knew about the house claim. Yue watched them find the numbers they needed and thought that public access looked very little like a celebration. Mostly it looked like someone being able to go home before dark.

archive_03_056.speaker: narrator
archive_03_056.text: Dai stood at the locked deposit screen and counted the packets scheduled for temporary movement during beam replacement. She would need owners' replies for some and emergency terms for others if the work became urgent. She did not discuss them with the public readers. Yue carried the open-room stool list to the door. The hall contained both strangers and guarded papers without requiring one group to possess the other. For the first time she could imagine the winter room functioning again rather than existing as an argument on the grant application.

archive_03_057.speaker: narrator
archive_03_057.text: The repair carter came up to inspect his unloading route on the seventeenth day. He refused the inner ramp because rain had loosened its edge. The carpenter proposed a longer approach through the yard, requiring one temporary table to move and the public hour to shift. Luo agreed after a visibly painful pause. Dai wrote the changed time on the notice instead of announcing that access had been preserved unchanged. The safer route would take half a morning longer. The carpenter adjusted the schedule, keeping the estimate's permitted weather margin visible.

archive_03_058.speaker: narrator
archive_03_058.text: Sun encountered the revised notice while visiting the cook. She asked Luo whether he wanted her to give another public reading to make up for the closed hour. He began to accept before noticing how she watched him. Then he asked whether she actually wanted to read. She said she wanted the cook's pickle recipe and had offered because he looked miserable. He laughed and declined her remedy. She went into the kitchen, leaving him to solve a scheduling problem with scheduling rather than a retired woman's kindness.

archive_03_059.speaker: narrator
archive_03_059.text: The daybook assessment came back on the eighteenth afternoon. Several leaves could be separated safely, and the entry at issue remained readable. The visitor was He's mother. Luo had copied the house continuation clause for her fourteen years earlier and directed her to the orchard trustees for a legal answer. A marginal handling reference recorded the source being placed in an inner wrapper labelled school path because its previous folder had torn. The house paper had apparently been returned, but under a title that made its private consequence disappear inside a public agreement.

archive_03_060.speaker: narrator
archive_03_060.text: The report did not deliver the house paper itself. It supplied a dated location lead and a careful transcription of the enquiry. He received the permitted report with his mother present. She recognised the visit date by a child she had carried on her back: He, then too young to remember the archive stairs. He stared at the entry in which his mother had become a visitor requesting an answer. She had made the journey. Someone had copied the clause. The trustees had replied later that the original gave no descendant right. An entire small history stood between those sentences.

archive_03_061.speaker: narrator
archive_03_061.text: Luo apologised for directing her to the trustees without recording a follow-up that would have preserved the conflicting texts. At the time he had thought his duty ended after supplying the copy. He remembered wanting the reading room to serve more people than it could seat. The mother said the direction itself had been useful; the missing follow-up had made it easier for the later refusal to sound final. She accepted the apology as a statement, not as settlement. Luo wrote the follow-up failure beside Dai's broken move reference.

archive_03_062.speaker: narrator
archive_03_062.text: The school-path packet was among documents already admitted for public consultation, but it had several inner wrappers. Tan opened the identified wrapper under support while Dai checked its older tie description. The house continuation paper lay behind the public agreement, folded twice and bearing the registrar's endorsement missing from He's retained copy. Its text matched the descendant condition. A separate annotation, however, recorded a later revision request whose outcome was not attached. Finding an original ended the search for that object and immediately opened a search for what had happened to its legal force.

archive_03_063.speaker: narrator
archive_03_063.text: He let out one laugh so abrupt that his mother flinched. Then he read the revision annotation and stopped. The representative examined the endorsed clause without claiming the request had necessarily annulled it. A request was not a completed act. Dai recorded the recovered location and the reason it had been missed, preserving every earlier error entry. Yue copied the relevant text into the comparison sheet. Her pen trembled slightly. She had expected a missing paper to feel like an answer. It felt instead like a door they could finally open without knowing the room beyond.

archive_03_064.speaker: he_xi
archive_03_064.text: I am trying very hard not to call this our house. There is a man living there, there is a request we have not traced, and I have just heard everyone say those things plainly. But for fourteen years my mother was told to behave as if the later clause had never existed. Today it is here. I need someone to let that be good before we turn it into the next difficult task. I do not need you to promise the key. I need one minute.

archive_03_065.speaker: narrator
archive_03_065.text: Dai gave him the minute. The representative looked out the window. Luo closed the comparison book without shutting the supported original. Yue watched the rain make distinct circles in the yard puddle. No one spoke until He took a breath and asked what a lawful revision would leave behind. Dai explained the registry trail and the notices ordinarily required for an affected tenancy. They would ask the district land registrar for those records. The inquiry belonged to a competent office; the archive could supply the recovered source and its custody history.

archive_03_066.speaker: narrator
archive_03_066.text: The beam materials arrived while the revision inquiry was being prepared. Ordinary events had not paused for the rediscovered instrument. The carter followed the inspected yard route, the workers stacked slates below the safe load marks and the carpenter checked the beam timber before accepting the invoice. Yue took receipt counts to the clerk and then returned to finish the admitted extract. Her day divided between two kinds of weight: the measured load of roof materials and the consequence of a paragraph that had spent years behind the wrong paper wrapper.

archive_03_067.speaker: narrator
archive_03_067.text: That night Dai and Luo faced the winter operating plan. The repaired hall could remain useful only if heat, food and paid people lasted through periods when the road closed. Their board would meet in a week. Tan wanted a preservation plan that did not fill the safe tables with damp packets, and the school wanted the path kept clear. The inheritance hearing would need witnesses who had their own autumn work. It was her nineteenth day; Yue had seventeen calendar days left in her first appointment. She could not perform every preliminary task before the board met.

archive_03_068.speaker: narrator
archive_03_068.text: Luo put three work requests on the table for Yue's next paid stretch. One involved the endowment and public access records needed for the winter board. Another concerned the ordinary path work and people who might volunteer bounded evidence before seasonal departures. The third involved Tan's move plan and practical winter room preparation. Each request had a staff lead and would continue without Yue, but her available hours could strengthen only one of the initial reports. Dai asked her to choose after breakfast, once she had slept.

archive_03_069.speaker: narrator
archive_03_069.text: Yue looked at the recovered house paper resting on its support behind the closed workroom door. Its late revision question remained open; the school stove was working; the roof materials had arrived; winter was becoming a problem with quantities rather than a word on a notice. She could compare the public use commitments, help collect specific path evidence or prepare the safe winter movement. Whichever task she joined, the other leads would need to report their own findings when the board assembled. She folded her day list and set it beside her untouched supper bowl.

choices.text: Compare the public access commitments and endowment records with Luo.
Help seek volunteered evidence of the school path with He and the clerk.
Prepare the safe winter rooms and movement plan with Tan.
